title: Hangxiety: Why some people experience anxiety after drinking alcohol
description:
After drinking alcohol, some people don’t just have a headache - they feel guilt, dread, low mood and a deep sense of embarrassment.

It’s known as ‘hang-xiety’ or hangover anxiety, and science backs up that it’s a real phenomenon. Alcohol affects all systems in the body, including the brain. so it can cause psychological symptoms.

Millie Gooch, author of Hangxiety and speaker breaks down how the nervous system and brain are impacted when the effects of alcohol wear off. She also tells us how hangxiety played a role in her sobriety journey.

We also hear about some people’s experience with anxiety, and how it changed their relationship with alcohol.

summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, host Hannah Gelbart explores 'hangxiety'—the feelings of anxiety, guilt, and dread that many people experience after drinking alcohol. Guest Millie Gooch, author of Hangxiety, explains the brain chemistry behind the phenomenon: alcohol initially stimulates GABA (the brain's calming neurotransmitter) and suppresses glutamate (the chemical that keeps us alert). When the effects wear off, the brain recalibrates, triggering a spike in glutamate and a drop in GABA, which causes post-drinking anxiety and low mood. Alcohol also affects memory formation and the prefrontal cortex, leading to memory blackouts and impulsive decisions. To reduce hangxiety, experts advise drinking smaller amounts more slowly, eating before drinking, and alternating alcoholic drinks with non-alcoholic options.
